correctness.rationale: The Gaussian Fourier formula gives exact entire identity I=2exp(-s|ξ|²)(cosh(q|ξ|²)+cos(h·ξ)). Expanding produces Q=4s Id+hh^T and the stated homogeneous quartic. In dimension d≥2 the rank-one part has a zero eigenvalue, so min(Q) determines s. The nullspace of T yields q² exactly; T determines the separation vector up to sign. Explicit reverse construction validates every listed feasible jet including h=0 and q=0; varying q fixes all lower jets; two verified rational d=1 examples share Q=9 and P4=31/3. The attached checker tests rational expansions, but infinite proof is algebraic.

value.rationale: The theorem is a natural complete inverse-data classification: for all separations it identifies the entire feasible fourth-order Fourier-intensity jet variety, yields explicit constructive two-scale inversion, proves sharp jet-order necessity and a nontrivial dimension-one failure by exact collision. Its use of a rank-one anisotropic covariance to isolate the Gaussian width sum provides a structural explanation of why 2D and higher differ from 1D. No general noise robustness is claimed.
